extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (postdocs, early-career researchers, and faculty seeking funding advice)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice and evaluative criteria for assessing fundability, interpreting review outcomes (impact scores, paylines, status changes), and deciding next steps for NIH grant applications across mechanisms (K, R, SBIR) during budget uncertainty and resubmission cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact program officer (PO) after receiving summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you receive your summary statement, contact your Program Officer to ask about next steps (e.g., whether to prepare an A1 application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO can advise on whether you should submit a resubmission and next steps; however, the PO often cannot confirm whether you will receive an award until the IC receives its federal appropriation. Introduce yourself to a newly assigned PO (always a good idea) and send updates (new publications, accepted abstracts, milestones) that might help internal discussions about ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret impact score relative to paylines and FOA specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: An impact score alone (especially without a percentile) must be interpreted in the context of IC-specific paylines, FOA/programmatic priorities, and whether a percentile is reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some FOAs (e.g., COVID-designated) may not report percentiles. Even without a percentile, a score can be 'within the zone of consideration' — check with PO. Different ICs and specific research focuses (e.g., ADRD) can have different interim funding lines; if your work fits a special focus, a different payline may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic priorities can override/modify score-based funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions consider programmatic priorities in addition to peer review scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially for targeted FOAs (e.g., COVID-19), ICs may use programmatic judgment rather than scores alone. Discuss with your PO how program priorities may affect your application's chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait for the summary statement before seeking detailed PO advice
rubrics_metrics.description: You should generally wait until you receive the summary statement to contact the PO about specific advice and next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements contain reviewer critiques that inform whether to resubmit and how to respond. Once you have the summary statement, the PO can better advise if a resubmission (A1) is appropriate or whether to prepare a new A0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission best practice: revise substantively in response to critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: When resubmitting (A1) or submitting a new A0 after a prior score, do not submit the exact same proposal; revise in response to reviewer critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, an A1 R15 scored outside the payline could be re-submitted as an A0, but it is strongly recommended to revise based on the A1 critiques rather than submitting 'exactly the same proposal.' For resubmissions, include a clear introduction addressing prior concerns where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit Just-in-Time (JIT) materials unless requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold off on submitting JIT materials until the PO or Grants Management Specialist requests them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMS staff may briefly open files to check for JIT and then revert status; premature JIT is unnecessary. Wait for an explicit request to submit JIT documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand status changes: 'Pending administrative review' vs 'Council review completed'
rubrics_metrics.description: A change to 'Pending administrative review' often means a GMS opened the file (e.g., to check JIT); a revert to 'Council review completed' can simply indicate no further administrative items were present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief status toggle does not necessarily mean a final decision; it often reflects routine processing. If JIT was requested, it suggests the application is being processed for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate funding timing delays tied to federal appropriations and fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Final award decisions and NoAs depend on when the federal budget/appropriation is signed into law; ICs typically take weeks/months to process awards after appropriations are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds flow HHS → NIH → ICs and are subject to administrative skimming; expect 6–8+ weeks (or longer) after budget enactment before awards are issued. There is typically a lull in awards around Oct–Nov as ICs close out the FY. Continuing Resolutions (CRs) delay awards further.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-level paylines change with budgets and pandemic-related demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines may hold steady, improve, or worsen depending on IC appropriations, the number/quality of applications, and pandemic-related budget pressures (e.g., extending current awardees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, K award paylines dropped in FY21 in part due to funds needed to support current awardees during the pandemic. POs may advise resubmission if paylines are expected to tighten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use IC-specific historical paylines and trends to set expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate past paylines and funding patterns at the specific IC for your mechanism to gauge fundability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH Reporter and PO conversations can help. Even if past years show a stable payline, year-to-year changes may occur due to applicant pool size/quality and budget constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR score interpretation is IC-specific; consult the PO
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a 'decent' score for SBIR/STTR (e.g., 28) varies by IC and year; direct consultation with your PO and knowledge of IC trends is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No one can guarantee funding until appropriation decisions; however, some scores (e.g., high 20s) may be 'better than average' depending on the IC and available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards are made to institutions, not individuals; transfer policies depend on mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH grants are awards to institutions. Research project grants (R01) are commonly transferred with the PI; education/training grants (R25) are institution-specific and typically cannot be moved without institutional relinquishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R25s, the original institution can name a new PI or decline the award. For R01s, institutions usually allow the PI to take the award, but transfer requires institutional agreements and can cause delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: If your mentor/institution will change between submission and award, disclose and document changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer panels may know about planned mentor moves; you should not pretend a transition won't occur — provide clear documentation and plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include changing primary mentor, adding co-mentors who will remain, submitting post-submission materials to address change of institute, and securing strong letters of support from the receiving institution. Discuss plans with your PO; they may allow post-submission materials to document transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99-specific eligibility and career-market disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are actively applying/interviewing for faculty positions, POs and panels may consider you no longer in need of mentored K99 support; disclosing job-market activity can affect award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs expect K99 to support trainees who still require mentored training. If you admit to being on the faculty job market, POs have reported that applicants are sometimes no longer considered for K99 awards. Consider alternatives (R01, MIRA, DP2, other K mechanisms) if you're already competitive for faculty positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a planned primary mentor moves, secure alternative mentoring/training arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your primary mentor plans to move, find a co-mentor at your current institution (or change the primary mentor) and obtain supporting letters describing training and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the training environment, faculty, and trainee pool. If a move undermines the originally reviewed environment, provide letters and modifications that demonstrate a robust alternative training plan. Discuss options with your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: When prior proposed aims become published before resubmission, update the application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Aim (e.g., Aim 1) is published prior to resubmission, revise the application to expand or modify aims rather than re-proposing already-completed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight latest publications and explain how you will build beyond published results; reviewers do not want identical, already-completed projects on resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: When POs advise resubmission due to budget/CR uncertainties, contemplate timing and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: POs may recommend resubmitting if continuing resolutions or budget uncertainty are likely to stall funding decisions and your score is borderline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a CR persists, a March resubmission (A1) or even a new A0 may be advisable. Confirm COVID-related extensions to eligibility and whether a new submission window is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative funding mechanisms if eligibility is ending or K is risky
rubrics_metrics.description: If K99 eligibility is nearly exhausted or funding is uncertain, consider other awards (R01, MIRA, DP2, K22, K01/K08/K25, K12) to launch independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss with your PO and mentor which awards align with your career stage and project; sometimes skipping a K and pursuing R-level funding is appropriate for those ready for independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: If PO is unresponsive or you have unusually long silence, escalate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: When you have not received substantive PO communication for an unusually long time after council review, consider contacting the Branch Chief for an update and advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branch Chiefs (e.g., for postdoctoral, early career programs) can sometimes provide clarity when PO communication is lacking. Use escalation judiciously and only after reasonable follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: You may cite an application as 'being processed for award' only with PO confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PO confirms your application is being processed (e.g., JIT requested or 'Pending administrative review'), you can cautiously cite this in other contexts, but nothing is guaranteed until the NoA is in hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to indicate funding status for an external nomination or deadline, check with your PO whether it is appropriate to cite the pending award and whether the NoA might arrive in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section (SRG) reassignment: optional study group requests are usually fine to leave blank
rubrics_metrics.description: You can leave optional study section requests blank; if your application is assigned to a different SRG, contact staff if reassignment back to the original panel is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRGs can be reorganized; if you see assignment to a different SRG in eRA Commons and believe reassignment is warranted, contact staff early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor NIH Reporter and IC award announcements for signals about funding patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Watching NIH Reporter and recent awards can give you a sense of which projects/mechanisms are being funded at an IC and help set expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see similar K or R awards being made, that can be an encouraging signal, but it does not guarantee your application's outcome. Use this as one input among PO advice and summary statement critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be strategic about contact timing and content with PO when new information arises
rubrics_metrics.description: When you have timing issues (e.g., funding gaps, appointment expiration) or new milestones (publications, accepted abstracts), convey these concisely to the PO to inform priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have an imminent appointment end or other stresses, inform the PO — this can help them advise on whether award timing or resubmission is critical. Keep communications factual and not excessive to avoid annoyance.
